articleTitle: Study on an expert monitoring system used for PD on-line monitoring of large turbine generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, a newly developed generator partial discharge (PD) expert monitoring system is presented. The system consists of four major modules, including system control module, system menu module, signal processing module and result display module. The system is based on expert system technique. Operators can process PD on-line monitoring more easily and automatically. Some field PD on-line monitoring results are also given and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Internal charge generation in polyvinylidene fluoride films during poling observed by Raman spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The electrical degradation and charge generation in PVDF during poling has been investigated using Raman spectroscopy. Two new peaks at 1118 cm/sup -1/ and 1515 cm/sup -1/ corresponding to conjugated polyene sequences arise in the Raman spectrum after poling. In conjunction with our observation that HF gas is formed during poling at the negative electrode, a HF-unzipping chain reaction initiated by F/sup -/-ions is proposed. The large amount of HF which can be generated by this mechanism might be a source for additional ionic charges if the HF molecules dissociate into H/sup +/- and F/sup -/-ions. Thus these additional charges could lead to a complete internal polarization neutralization even if the amount of injected charges is too small for this.

articleTitle: Chaotic character of luminous and partial discharge phenomena during ac electrical tree propagation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: We report that the characteristics of luminous intensity and current pulse of partial discharges during tree propagation in PMMA specimens can be analyzed simultaneously using the idea of chaos.

articleTitle: Preliminary study on the methods for suppressing background interference in ultra-wideband partial discharge detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The interferences often appear in partial discharge detection. Many methods have been developed to suppress interference. In order to decrease the influence of background signal on the frequency-domain analysis and to observe the characteristic peaks of the measured signal easier, we have studied some simple practical methods to suppress the background signals in ultra-wideband partial discharge detection. Sampled signals include discharge background noise, so a method to extract the discharge signal for frequency spectrum analysis was designed. And a D-value Method is also designed to process the signal data before and after discharge respectively. After data processing, a frequency spectrum of the discharge signal is available. It is obvious in practical use that these methods can suppress background interference effectively.

articleTitle: Coating effect on AC and impulse breakdown stress of SF/sub 6/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Under a uniform electric field and high (0.3 MPa) gas pressure, sulfur hexafluoride (SF/sub 6/) gas insulation breakdown strength was measured. When the coating is so thick that the electrical stress concentration caused by surface roughness is almost negligible, the breakdown stress for AC and impulse voltage is respectively 30/spl sim/88% and 18/spl sim/40% higher than that with bare electrodes. Breakdown stress dependence on the coating thickness and the electrode materials is discussed.

articleTitle: An investigation on DC conduction in ceramic capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Long term leakage currents in BaTiO/sub 3/ based multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCs) with and without polarity reversal at room temperature and 225/spl deg/C were measured, and comparison was made between these conduction results. It is shown that charges are injected and accumulated near the electrode/dielectric interface of MLC at room temperature, while ions are transported and accumulated near the cathode at elevated temperature. Also, the DC conduction current can be dominated by different conduction processes due to the change of migration ion density in bulk which changes with temperature. It is considered that the relationship between the space charge accumulation and conduction process discussed here will be useful to study the electrical properties of dielectric materials.

articleTitle: The development of the linear Rogowski coil for measuring large impulse current
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper describes the theory, design of the linear Rogowski coil, and analyzes its properties. The testing results show that it can measure not only large impulse (or power-frequency) current but also distributing impulse current on tabulate conductor. The rise time of this coil is about several nanoseconds, and its structure is simple. So it can be well used.

articleTitle: Development of DSP measuring system of high-field dielectric property of silicone rubber sheets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: We have developed a measuring system of high-field dielectric property with using FFT analysis. It is an application of digital signal processing technique to a conventional current comparator type capacitance bridge (CCB) system. In this paper, we introduce a digital signal processing (DSP) board into the mentioned dielectric measuring system. An analysis of surface property of silicone rubber sheet is possible by using this system. It can measure the high-field dielectric property when the sample changes its surface property by drying in air and by wetting with water absorption.

articleTitle: Light spectra on DC corona
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The present paper has carried out an experiment on a test setup of needle-plate electrodes under DC voltage. Raising the applied voltage gradually, the corona spectra from the onset streamer to the breakdown streamer have been measured, The measured spectra range from 300 nm to 800 nm. The experiment has shown some regularities of corona spectra. For example, the UV spectra appears first when raising applied voltage gradually, then the longer wavelength spectra appear. Furthermore, compared with those spectra measured on a long air gap by the Les Renardieres Group, some new spectral wavelengths have been found. These results are of important significance both in theory and practice of insulation monitoring.

articleTitle: Development of new electrode system for measurement of high field dielectric properties near breakdown field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In order to study the high field AC conduction mechanism near breakdown field, a new electrode system was developed using an evaporated polypropylene (PP) guard film. Using this technique high field dielectric properties of a biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) film near breakdown field could be measured. The improved new electrode system enables the measurement of tan/spl delta/ in an electric field region 100kV/sub rms//mm higher than for the usual method, because there are no air voids between the sample film and the evaporated PP guard film. Furthermore we could measure the tan/spl delta/ and the dissipation current to about 270 kV/sub rms//mm, using a fast rising AC ramp voltage application technique.

articleTitle: Research on the PTC properties of polyethylene/carbon black composites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The influence of carbon black and polyethylene on the conductance and the PTC properties of polyethylene/carbon black composites is investigated. I-V characteristics of the composite are also measured. Experimental results show that the PTC properties of a sample containing carbon black are not evident and the conductance of the composite is attributed to the tunneling current of intergrain gaps between carbon black particles. The phase change model is used to explain the phenomenon of PTC and NTC well.

articleTitle: Partial discharges and surface potential at fissure-like solid-solid interface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Surface potentials at fissure-like interface formed by two epoxy resin blocks were studied after PD occurring in air gap in series with the interface at the room temperature. The negative potential was detected at the zero-cross point of ac applied voltage from negative to positive after negative PD occurred during the previous negative half-cycle and the positive potential was detected in the reverse case. Surface potentials, caused by charge deposition from PD, were found having a close relation to PD magnitude. Comparing the positive surface potential to the negative one, their surface potential values and distributions on the interface had some differences. Different PD statuses between positive PD and negative PD are thought to be one of the important factor Positive PD are considered to crawl into the interface through the air gap from the needle-electrode while applied voltage increased and positive surface potentials as well as PD characteristics were susceptible to the surface roughness. Roughened surfaces are supposed to have a higher capacity of charge deposition due to their higher surface potentials and wide gradual potential distributions on the roughened interface.

articleTitle: Relation between residual voltage ratio and microstructural parameters of ZnO varistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The effect of thickness on residual voltage ratio K/sub r/ of ZnO varistors is experimentally studied, which shows that a dimensional effect of K/sub r/ also exists. The relations are experimentally investigated between residual voltage ratio K/sub r/ and breakdown strength E/sub 1mA/, and K/sub r/ and microstructural parameters. It is shown that K/sub r/ decreases with E/sub 1mA/, and increases with average grain size /spl mu/. An integrated parameter the product of average grain size /spl mu/ and grain size variance /spl sigma//sup 2/ is found to be a better parameter to show the relation between electrical properties and microstructure of ZnO varistors. A microstructural model for simulation is proposed. By using computer, the relations are simulated between K/sub r/ and thickness, K/sub r/ and average grain size /spl mu/ & K/sub r/ and the product /spl sigma//sup 2//spl mu/. The simulated results are consistent with experimental ones.

articleTitle: Nomex paper T-411 impregnated with adhesive varnish and its application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The authors show that adhesive Nomex paper 411 has operated for a long time in many rotor coils of generators. It is of stable quality, they are going to push this product as a new insulating material to the market. Nomex insulating paper 411 is a non-rolled smooth paper, this kind of paper is of heat shrinkage and easy moisture absorption type. The paper will be extended both crosswise and longitudinally, so, it must be treated by heat-shrinkage before use, so as to avoid quality problems by shrinkage in application. Mechanical performance of non-rolled smooth paper Nomex 411 is not as good as 410, so the ideal applied state for adhesive Nomex paper is to treat it by heating extrusion and fixing in the structure, for instance, insulation between turns of magnetic pole coils in a synchronizer, so that it improves the mechanical strength.

articleTitle: Capacitance change during the aging of a combined system of a solid-liquid dielectric under switching impulse voltages
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper presents the result of an experimental investigation of the arising non-linear phenomena in bakelite and phenol impregnated pressboard specimens (pertinax), immersed in insulating oil, under the application of high voltage impulses. For this purpose, bakelite and pertinax samples were electrically stressed with 250/2500 /spl mu/s switching impulse voltages through a tip-plane electrode assembly. The total electric charge flow through the specimens and the overall capacitance C of the metal tip-solid dielectric-metal plane combination were measured in the high-field regime, the experimental results show an exponential increase of the overall capacitance which may be attributed to the excessive charge flow due to the electron avalanche effect. The aforementioned capacitance involved with the partial discharges depends on the environment temperature (partial discharges enhanced by temperature). Further theoretical consideration leads to a mathematical model which gives an expression for C. The theoretical expectations on the basis of this model are found to be in good agreement with the obtained experimental results.

articleTitle: Static electrification as an evaluation method of thermal aging in transformer oil
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The experimental results of static electrification of several kinds of thermally aged transformer oil are presented in this paper. A pure oil sample and four oil samples in presence of copper, pressboard, silicon steel sheet, copper+pressboard+silicon steel sheet respectively, have been aged at 110/spl deg/C under air condition. Static electrification measurement at different aged degree was carried out in a system with the sintered metal filter. The changes of static electrification are compared to classical aging indexes, such as loss factor (tan /spl delta/), conductivity (/spl gamma/) and acid number (AN). The experimental results show that static electrification has relationship with thermal aging and the sensitivity of classical indexes for thermal aging process is smaller than changes of static electrification.

articleTitle: Analysis of discharge currents with discernibility matrices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper the rough set theory which has been developed to derive the features of various coarse data was applied to the discharge currents accompanied by tree developments. The original current data were calculated to make a set of condition attributes at some time points and a decision attribute was also derived. The discernibility matrices presented by Skowron in the rough set theory were applied to the time dependent set of condition attributes and decision attribute to predict its future time series.

articleTitle: The voltage endurance of low density polyethylene with surface treated inorganic filler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The effect of surface-treated inorganic filler on the voltage-endurance of Low-Density Polyethylene has been investigated. The inorganic filler used for the test is clay which was treated by adding silane and high speed stirring at 60/spl sim/70/spl deg/C. Both LDPE with treated filler (filled LDPE) and LDPE without filler (unfilled LDPE) were used for voltage endurance, electrical breakdown and dielectric loss experiment. The experimental results show that the life index of filled-LDPE is higher than that of unfilled LDPE. As the aging time prolongs, the residual electrical breakdown strength of filled-LDPE increases and the dielectric loss factor (tan/spl delta/) of filled-LDPE decreases at 70/spl deg/C, respectively. On the base of experimental results, a deep electronic trap mechanism for the effect of inorganic filler treated with coupling agent is put forward. It is considered that the surface-treated filler with silane may supply deep electronic traps reducing the carrier mobility and carrier density in filled-LDPE to suppress electrical tree propagation. Thermally stimulated current (TSC) and electrical treeing experiments have been performed. The experimental results are consistent with theoretical analyses.

articleTitle: Detection of partial discharge in operating turbine generator using GHz-band spatial phase difference method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: We developed PD detection system based on "Spatial Phase Difference Method" for detecting microwave (GHz) emitted from PD. We applied the PD detection system to the off-line turbine generator in the regular overhaul and the on-line turbine generator that had two built-in antennas. The detection system was able to detect the microwave emitted from PD of a few 1000 pC in operating turbine generator.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of return voltage characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Recently the return voltage measurements have been proposed for the diagnostics on the high voltage equipment characterising the dielectric properties of insulation systems. The application of return voltage method at the diagnostics of the HV current transformers are presented in this paper. The return voltage characteristics such as a maximum of return voltage, the initial slope of return voltage and the time to peak value dependencies on charging time are discussed. These characteristics vary depending on the ageing changes of the insulation. That indicate for a possible applicability of the technique for assessing the state of transformer insulation. The investigations of temperature influence on the return voltage characteristics were aimed to determine the state of the insulation under operating conditions. The theoretical analysis of the results allows to calculate the temperature of insulation that corresponds to the thermal breakdown of insulation.

articleTitle: Development of partial discharge monitor for turbine generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: A new partial discharge (PD) monitor has been developed. It continuously monitors electrical condition of stator winding insulation of the turbine generators in service. Wires of a resistance temperature detector (RTD) preinstalled between top and bottom coils of a stator slot are used as a RF coupler so that no new device installed inside a generator is required. Electromagnetic noise occurring around the generator is rejected by detection with multiple sensors and signal processing software. Results of in-service measurements show negative load and temperature dependence of PD characteristic. It is expected that the dependence is a symptom of degradation of the insulation system.

articleTitle: A current sensor for insulator corona discharge measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Previously obtained results indicated that it could be a way to detect faulty insulators by measuring corona pulse current from the insulator string. This paper presents a pulse current sensor, with high sensitivity (/spl mu/A) and wide frequency band (7 kHz-25 MHz), developed for detecting pulse currents form insulator corona discharges on line. Through spectrum analysis of corona pulse currents produced by 110 kV-suspension insulator string, we found that the frequency band and 3-dB cutoff frequency of the corona pulse currents are respectively 17 MHz and 2.5 MHz. Based on the spectrum analysis, we developed a special designed Rogowski coil to detect corona currents on transmission line, which has a core made of super microcrystal material. We tested the core material and found that it is of high /spl mu/ value (magnetic permeability, >10000) and wide frequency characteristics (2 kHz-25 MHz). In order to make the best design, the influence of coil turns and integrating resistance on the frequency band and sensitivity of the sensor was investigated. It was found from the test that the sensitivity of the sensor changes with integrating resistance. The larger the integrating resistance is, the higher the sensitivity of the sensor is, and the narrower the frequency band of the sensor will be. The central frequency of the band changes with coil turns. The more the coil turns are, the lower the central frequency will be, the lower the sensitivity of the sensor will be, the lower the sensitivity of the sensor will be. Considering the sensitivity and on-site interference, the integrating resistance and coil turns are chosen as 100 /spl Omega/ and 25 MHz. The designed sensor was used to measure the corona pulse current produced by an insulator string by coupling from a ground wire of a tower in our laboratory. It is shown from the on-site that the sensor is very suitable to detecting corona pulse currents from insulator string in service.

articleTitle: Effect of cross magnetic field on solid, liquid, gaseous and biological dielectrics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: During the last three decades rapid advances in studies on the mechanism of ionization, conductivity and breakdown of dielectrics have been reported. These studies are closely linked with other very important fields of physics such as the physics of plasma in gases, the dosimetry of ionizing radiation, conductivity of materials, etc. Measurement of certain basic quantities connected with electrical conductivity such as coefficients of mobility, recombination and diffusion of ions or activation energy in different chemical compounds enable the microscopic values to be linked with microstructure of liquids. In the above studies the effect of a magnetic field on different dielectric materials has not often been reported. Dielectric materials as used in the field of science and technology are not only subjected to an electric field alone; quite often, they are under the influence of both electric and magnetic fields. In this paper the effect of both electric and magnetic fields on (i) pre-breakdown, breakdown, transport properties and activation energy of liquid dielectrics, (ii) ageing and surface breakdown of solid dielectrics in vacuum and low pressure gaseous discharge and (iii) internal field and polarization of biological dielectrics have been reviewed, discussed and future applications predicted.

articleTitle: Prebreakdown light emission in liquid helium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, the observation results of the prebreakdown light emission phenomena under divergent fields in liquid helium are reported. Two structures of light emission, filamentary and bush-like, were found for both positive and negative polarities. Most of the negative light emission should a filamentary structure, while it was a bush-like one for the positive. Light emission appeared for only a few microseconds for negative needle, while it lasts much longer than 25 /spl mu/s for positive needle. The pulse frequency of the light emission differed between the polarities.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the dependencies between PD in polyethylene insulation and treeing fractal characteristics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Exploitation of equipment with polyethylene (PE) insulation requires condition monitoring and diagnostics. Traditionally diagnostics of insulation condition is carried out by means of partial discharges (PD) registration. There are a number of works that allow identification of the defect by the PD method. However, such identification of defects, for example, voids, inclusions or treeing, does not show the danger from the point of view of full insulation gap breakdown and insulation construction failure. Information about the form and size of defects formed on high voltage treeing is necessary for prediction of the remained resources of PE insulation. For this purpose we carry out experimental research for determination of the dependencies of PD characteristics in PE upon electrical stress and fractal dimension of corresponding treeing. The investigations were carried out by means of electrical measurement of PD current and simultaneous optical recording of treeing form.

articleTitle: Study on the ultra-wideband characteristics of some typical interference signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: As is well known the accuracy and credibility of partial discharge measurement might be influenced seriously by surrounding interference. Using the technique of ultra-wideband partial discharge detection, we have studied the characteristics of some typical period interference and random interferences, including brush discharge interference, operating high-voltage interference, operating computer interference, rectifier interference and so on. The experimental results that the characteristics of these interferences can be distinguished either in time-domain or in frequency-domain, particularly, based on the characteristic frequency peak and the shape of characteristic peak by using digital analysis technique. It is helpful for the development of the insulation diagnosis technique.

articleTitle: Electrical treeing as a mechanically driven phenomenon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Over the past few years a body of experimental evidence has accumulated which supports the hypothesis that the mechanical characteristics of an insulating material strongly influence electrical degradation mechanisms. Research has concentrated on the phenomenon of electrical treeing. This paper describes simple experiments in which the mechanical strength of electrical insulation was directly affected by plasticisation, followed by investigations of the influence of internal barriers and particulate fillers, and arriving at a proposed pre-stressed material (akin to pre-stressed concrete) which takes advantage of the results of this work in developing a mechanically and electrically enhanced insulating system.

articleTitle: Dielectric loss of BaTiO/sub 3/-based high voltage ceramic capacitor under high field strength
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: High voltage ceramic capacitors are widely used in high voltage power systems, because they have the merits of small volume, high voltage endurance and low aging. However, high dielectric loss will heat the capacitor under high field strength, and reduce the stability and reliability of capacity. In this paper, results for decreasing dielectric loss under high field strength was reported. It is shown that suitable recipes and technology can decrease dielectric loss and improve the reliability of high voltage ceramic capacitor under high field strength.

articleTitle: Observation of AC surface discharge dynamic behavior under various atmosphere pressure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The surface discharge dynamic behavior under various atmospheric pressures (200 mmHg-1000 mmHg) is observed by using the advanced 2-D image lock-in amplifier technique of E-O (electro-optical) Pockels effect.

articleTitle: Partial discharge detection and location in cable joint
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Compared with the electrical measurement of discharge, acoustic measurement of discharge has advantages in noise reduction and location of partial discharge sites. In this paper, a sensitive acoustic emission (AE) sensor is used to pick up ultrasonic signals produced by partial discharge in laboratory made polyethylene (PE) samples and an extruded-cable joint under high voltage were studied.

articleTitle: Thermal decomposition characteristics of DGEBA/MDA/GN system for insulating materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this study, the thermal decomposition activation energy of diglycidyl ether of bisphenol A(DGEBA)/4,4'-methylene dianiline (MDA) system toughened with glutaronitrile (GN) was calculated by thermal decomposition characteristics and their thermal stability was estimated.

articleTitle: Effect of surface charges on impulse flashover voltages of spacer in SF/sub 6/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The positive and negative charges were injected onto the spacer surface by DC corona discharges, and the flashover characteristics were investigated by a sudden change from DC to lightning or steep-fronted impulse in the presence of a conducting-particle attached on the spacer in SF/sub 6/ gas. Experimental results showed that the polarity of corona charges has a great influence on impulse flashover voltages. For the opposite polarity impulse to corona charges, there is a significant shift of the time domain where the minimum flashover voltage appears in the U-shaped curves of relationships between flashover voltage and wavefront duration (U/sub f/-t/sub f/). Also, the influence of DC polarity reversal on the corona discharge current has been studied.

articleTitle: An interface testing cell for multi-stress ageing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: With the wider introduction of solid insulating material combinations in components, problems have become apparent at their interfaces. In order to study and to test interfaces, testing cells are being developed in which an electric field can be applied partly along the interface of two solid dielectrics. The present paper presents a sample cell that is suitable for two materials that can rub along each other and make discharging likely at the interface. This effect is believed to have contributed to several major failures. The cell is also fit for investigating environmental influences. The paper outlines interface degradation; describes the requirements, design and use of the sample cell; reports the first exploratory experiments.

articleTitle: DC insulating properties of newly developed XLPE cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: We have conducted a study into the application of high density polyethylene (HDPE) to DC cable insulation. HDPE has excellent electrical properties under DC voltage. However, it appeared that HDPE is very difficult to use for DC cable insulation because of a production problem where HDPE easily generates voids, in which case the insulation wall thickness increases. We studied past experimental knowledge again, and investigated the development of new DC power cable insulation.

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics of gaseous and liquid nitrogen in parallel plane electrodes system with small gap spacer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: To design the electrical insulation for a superconducting magnet cooled by liquid nitrogen or liquid helium measurements were carried out on the DC breakdown voltage of gas or liquid nitrogen with and without a GFRP spacer. The results are summarized as follows: Breakdown voltages are determined by the product of the cryogenic nitrogen gas density and electrode distance when a spacer is inserted between the electrodes tightly without apparent gap. When a small gap is introduced, the breakdown occurs along the surface of the spacer or in the vicinity of the spacer. The surface breakdown occurs below the gap breakdown voltage. In liquid nitrogen, bubbles stagnate on the spacer surface and surface breakdown occurs below the breakdown voltage of liquid nitrogen at the presence of the spacer between electrodes.

articleTitle: Research on on-line PD monitoring system for large power transformer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper presents a new set of on-line partial discharge (PD) monitoring system for large power transformer. Four sets of 500 kV power transformers can be monitored automatically at the same time, and then fault warning and localization are made by software. Various methods are used to reject interference in order to increase the monitoring sensitivity of PD. The on-line calibration technique, the pulse injection through capacitive tapping, is applied for measurement of apparent discharge. The earthing fault of transformer was found while the system commissioning. Now this system has been in operation steadily for more than two years. As one of main prevision maintenance testing item, on-line PD monitoring systems are paid more attention by engineers both in China and abroad. Up to now, some on-line systems had already been put in operation in Canada, Japan and China. They have already got many good results and accumulating a lot of good experiences. On base of summarizing forefather's works, a new type of JFY-2 on-line PD monitoring system for large power transformer has been developed by Jilin electric power research institute joint with Tsinghua university.

articleTitle: Analytical computation of the transfer functions of transformers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper presents the application of an analytical method for the computation of the transfer functions of transformers. The method used shows in contrast to other procedures no principal limits in the considered frequency range and calculates iteratively both the structure of the transfer function as well as the system parameters. For this reason, the transfer function of any transformer can be computed automatically, thus enabling the presented method to be the base for a diagnosis of the operating behaviour of the devices. The suitability of the applied method is shown by a comparison of measured frequency responses and calculated transfer functions of a distribution transformer as well as of a power transformer.

articleTitle: Effect of surface roughness on potential distribution of dielectric materials after partial discharge exposure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The purpose of this study is to clarify the factor of the appearance of Swarming Pulsive Microdischarges (SPMD). For this end, the surface potential distribution of dielectric materials after partial discharge (PD) exposure and its time dependence were measured in connection with surface roughness.

articleTitle: Use of FFT and ANN techniques in monitoring of transformer fault gases
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper reports on continuing work undertaken by the authors in developing a portable monitor to detect multigases especially H/sub 2/ and CO dissolved in oil. A significant improvement in reliability of detection has been achieved using FFT and ANN signal processing techniques. The monitor uses the membrane and forced diffusion techniques to extract the dissolved gases in oil, and senses the gases by two thin film semiconducting gas sensors. Stability in sensor detection especially in a practical varying ambient conditions is achieved by a cyclic heating technique. And ac conductance measurement technique. Sensitivity and quantitative selectivity are achieved by signal processing using FFT and ANN techniques. The FFT resolves the frequency components of the sensor response up to 3rd harmonics and the data are used to train a back propagation ANN network to map the fingerprints. Detection up to 20 ppm has been achieved by just using two sensors. Detection for other gases like C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ and CO/sub 2/ has been done by using different membranes using the same two sensors and the measured response will be reported. A portable microcontroller based monitor was developed by incorporating in software the derived weights of ANN and the measuring techniques. The results are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: The sensitivity of identify faulty insulator string by detecting insulator corona current
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Some basic study indicated that detecting insulator corona pulse current could be a way to inspect for the faulty insulator string in service. The basic principle of identifying the faulty insulators in the string will cause a high voltage drop across good insulators due to their low resistance, producing active corona discharges on good insulators. The further study was conducted in our laboratory to examine the measuring sensitivity of identifying the faulty insulator string by detecting insulator corona current.

articleTitle: Triboelectrification of oil flow in pipelines adjacent to ac power transmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper introduces an experimental investigation into the effect of proximity of petrol pipelines to ac power transmission lines on electrostatic charging tendency (ECT) of flowing oil using a reduced-scale model. Simultaneous measurements of the applied ac voltage to the wire, pipe floating potential, corona current and streaming current of the flowing oil are achieved. The results reveal that conductor bundling has a monumental impact on all the measured quantities. In addition, oil temperature causes evident quantitative as well as qualitative changes in the measured streaming current, while as it has no effect on both pipe floating potential and corona current. The proximity of such pipelines to ac power transmission lines induces higher voltages in the pipelines and hence higher ECT of the flowing oil, especially at high temperature. Consequently, the explosion and fire hazards increase for such pipelines. Electric field computation shows that a higher number of subconductors leads to a nonlinear increase in both absolute electric field at the ground level and pipe floating potential.

articleTitle: A multi-resolution system approach to power transformer insulation diagnosis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Based on the synthetic analysis of the cause and serious degree of transformer faults, a decision tree method is presented, its identification order is from up to down, and each leaf of the decision tree represents a kind of fault model. The classification machine of different branches of decision tree is composed of different artificial neural network (ANN), thus a system model of combinatorial ANN is constructed, and the multi-resolution identification for transformer faults is achieved. The shortage of the complex configuration and the slow convergence of single ANN is overcome with this method, and the diagnosis accuracy is improved simultaneously. The application results show that this method is valuable for transformer faults diagnosis.

publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma

articleTitle: A method for calculating low probability impulse breakdown voltages in SF/sub 6/-filled gaps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: From the analysis of the abnormal discharge in SF/sub 6/-filled gaps, a method for calculating low probability impulse breakdown voltage is put forward, which consists of three limiting lines: the streamer breakdown line, the low probability impulse breakdown level and the streamer onset line in different gas pressure ranges. The calculated value gives a safety margin compared with the measured value.

articleTitle: Estimation method of nanometer order density distribution of polyethylene with an energy filtering TEM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: One-dimensional mass-thickness distribution of polyethylene specimen was estimated with an energy-filtering TEM for unstained specimen with suitable calibration points using lamella information as calibration data. Possibility to estimate the free volume ratio distribution and therefore the possibility of free volume distribution itself becomes realistic. Free volume ratio is the average free volume amount along the electron beam line across TEM specimen and it is not free volume distribution itself. We need proper definition of "Free Volume Distribution" for further development.

articleTitle: Influence of radiation environments on space charge formation in /spl gamma/-irradiated LDPE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Space charge profiles have been observed directly in irradiated LDPE using the PEA technique. There are marked differences between the charge characteristics of material irradiated in air and in vacuum and oxygen-free nitrogen gas. It is evident that the presence of oxygen during irradiation is essential for a significant amount of space charge to form in the irradiated LDPE. At low applied stress, a large amount of positive charges are present in the sample irradiated in air while only a small amount of charges exist in the samples irradiated in vacuum and oxygen-free nitrogen gas. At high applied stress charge injection takes place. In the case of samples irradiated in air, electrons injected neutralise with the positive ions, leading to significant reduction in space charge density. At low applied stress, space charge remaining in the sample can be used to assess the ageing taking place in the material.

articleTitle: Effect of liquid impregnation on ac and impulse tree initiation in XLPE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: XLPE was impregnated with 4 kinds of dielectric liquids to fill up large (>several 10 nm) free volume. This treatment removes space for electrons to be accelerated to high energy. The experimental results show that liquid impregnation drastically increases ac tree resistance of XLPE, but it does not change impulse characteristics.

articleTitle: New digital calibrator with impressed current pulses for partial discharge measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, a new digital calibrator for partial discharge (PD) measurements is presented. This generator works with impress well specified charges. Thus, in difference to conventional calibrators used until now, the generated calibration pulses show only minimal dependencies both from the interior electronic realisation of the calibrator as well as from the measuring object. Because of the digital storage, the pulse shapes are adaptable to nearly every measuring system. A comparison of real PD pulses injected in a transformer coil with the pulse shapes of both the new calibrator and of conventional generators injected in the same coil shows, that the signals from the new generator are much more similar to the real PD pulses. Thus, with the new generator pulses with nearly any shape and charge adjustable in wide range can be injected in high voltage devices.

articleTitle: Breakdown experiment in compound material of epoxy resin base
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this research, a needle-plate electrode system is adopted and the initial voltage of partial discharge, breakdown under electrical and thermal aging process, and the pattern of partial discharge during electrical aging are tested. The mechanism of the material breakdown and discharge is studied combining the analysis of microphotographs of the material.

articleTitle: New organic light-emitting-diodes using benzoxazole derivatives
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The authors synthesized new fluorescent dyes with benzoxazole group and evaluated the electroluminescent (EL) properties of organic light-emitting-diodes (OLED) with new dyes as emitting material. Our typical OLED showed a luminance of over 300 cd/m/sup 2/ at 10 V. However, the EL efficiencies of these OLEDs were not necessarily high. As these benzoxazole dyes have a triphenylamine group, holes easily flew out to cathode without hole-electron recombination. Then we synthesized a new benzoxazole dimer derivative without triphenylamine group.

articleTitle: Effect of ozone annealing on the charge trapping property of Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/-Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/-p-Si capacitor grown by low pressure chemical vapor deposition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The effects of ozone annealing on the trapping properties of Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ deposited by LPCVD have been examined. It is concluded that the ozone annealing efficiently eliminates electron traps existing throughout the Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ film but generates hole traps. Structural or stoichiometric change induced by the ozone annealing is suggested as a reason.

articleTitle: The use and evaluation of rapid screening method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This paper shows that there is an intimate relation between the TG data and long term thermal endurance of dielectrics. TG curves are able to reveal the thermochemical stability of the dielectrics and are main factors governing their thermal capability. But, they are in principle different from the thermal endurance properties of insulating materials again. This is chiefly because TG data are lacking in the functionality, that is, can not reflect the physical thermostability of materials, further, both reaction mechanisms have a certain differences as well. The paper still gives the comparison between rapid thermal endurance test methods and conventional aging method, and analyzes why errors of Cut line method are excessive.

articleTitle: Study of the effect of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ on the technique of casting system of epoxy resins
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, the influence of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ filler on the resin casting system is discussed. Two major factors, Na/sub 2/O content and the acid treatment, are investigated respectively. The surface nature of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ powder is also considered.

articleTitle: Study of the effects of coupling agents on the property of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-epoxy resin casting system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, the effects of two kinds of coupling agents, silicane and titanate, on the casting technology and mechanical property of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-epoxy resin system were studied. The results show that the filler can improve the impact strength of the casting system, after it was treated by silicane coupling agent. Additionally, it is helpful to improve the processing property of the casting system after the filler was added with a little titanate coupling agent. The mechanical performances of the cured resin were affected by the drying temperature of the post-treated filler too.

articleTitle: Synthesis and application of aragonite whisker
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Gas-liquid system was used to synthesize aragonite whiskers. The effect of temperature, pH value and accelerating agents were studied. Scanning electronic microscope (SEM) was used to observe the shape and size of whiskers. The contents of aragonite in the samples are determined by using X-ray diffraction. According to experiments, the best reacting conditions are found and aragonite whiskers with fine shape are synthesized.

articleTitle: Microwave dielectric properties of Ba(Mg,Ta)O/sub 3/-Ba(Co,Nb)O/sub 3/ ceramics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Ba(Mg,Ta)O/sub 3/-Ba(Co,Nb)O/sub 3/ ceramics were prepared by the conventional mixed oxide method. The ceramics were sintered at the temperature of 1500/spl sim/1575/spl deg/C for 5 hours in air. Ba(Mg,Ta)O/sub 3/-Ba(Co,Nb)O/sub 3/ ceramics have a structure of complex perovskite type, and have peaks of [101], [102], [201], [202] and [212]. In the case of the 0.7Ba(Mg,Ta)O/sub 3/-0.3Ba(Co,Nb)O/sub 3/ specimens sintered at 1550/spl deg/C for 5 hours, dielectric constant, duality factor and temperature coefficient of resonant frequency (TCRF, /spl tau//sub f/) were a good value of 27, 15, 712 at 11 GHz and -1.3 PPM//spl deg/C from 25/spl deg/C to 60/spl deg/C, respectively.

articleTitle: Study on thermal stability of non-halogen flame retardant polyolefin composite systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The effects of base resin, content of fillers and coupling agents on the thermal stability of non-halogen flame-retardant polyolefin composite have been investigated in this paper. In order to study the aging mechanism of the polyolefin composite systems, the fracture surfaces of aged specimens were observed by using scanning electron microscope (SEM). Based on the results, an effective way was put forward to enhance the thermal stability of non-halogen flame-retardant polyolefin composite systems.

articleTitle: Digest Report on the Investigating Committee on Interfacial Electronic Phenomena and Intellectual Properties of Organic Thin Films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma

articleTitle: An insert effect of insulation materials in plasma chemical reactions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Industrial applications for gas cleaning using a pulsed discharge plasma have been experimentally studied. The authors proposed a new nonthermal plasma process for reforming hydrocarbon fuel from methane by means of a concentric-cylinder-type reactor. This paper presents some experimental results of inserting a glass-fiber sheet between cathode and anode in the plasma chemical reactor. By inserting a glass-fiber sheet, production of hydrocarbon gases was enhanced compared with that without insulation material while input power was the same. Especially, ethylene production efficiency was much higher compared to the case with no insulation material.

articleTitle: The degradation of barium titanate (BaTiO/sub 3/) films under high electric fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper attention is directed toward the degradation and breakdown mechanism of the alkoxy-derived barium titanate (BaTiO/sub 3/) films in applied high electric field. Both ac and dc degradation are characterized by a large increase in conductivity. The lower breakdown voltage of the step method probably results from increased degradation rate due to longer applied field times. Studying dc degradation indicates that Schottky emission is a sign of unreliable dielectrics.

articleTitle: Depth dependence of modified bond on surface processed PTFE using high E/n discharge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The authors have studied on collision process in the discharge under high E/n conditions. From the results, it was deduced that many activated species are generated in the discharge. Using the discharge, surface processing of PTFE (Poly-Tetra-Fluoro-Ethylene) was carried out. As the result, a surface wettability was increased. During the processing, the sample on the cathode was irradiated by ions with kinetic energy. It is considered that these ions may implant into the surface. The range of ions in a sample is different from each molecule. Then, it is assumed that a wettability is not always increased by the processing, because the modification by ion occurs at different depth depending on mass of molecules. To make clear a difference of modification depth on PTFE, the processing was carried out using noble gases and the depth profile by the XPS analysis using the TOA (Take-Off-Angle) resolution was obtained. A result showed that the modified layer is relatively uniform using He gas and its density is lower than another noble gas.

articleTitle: The effects of dispersing state of Al(OH)/sub 3/ particles on dielectric properties of EPDM/Al(OH)/sub 3/ composite
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, the dispersing state of Al(OH)/sub 3/ particles in a EPDM matrix was observed with scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and the dispersing parameter was calculated on the base of Maxwell's theory and by using the equation generalized by Yamada. Moreover, the effects of the dispersing state of Al(OH)/sub 3/ particles on the dielectric properties of composites was also studied.

articleTitle: Study of non-linear electrical conductivity and anti-corona property of /spl beta/-SiC made from gangue
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The micro-powder of /spl beta/-SiC was synthesized from gangue. The influences of temperature, particle size and content of /spl beta/-SiC on the non-linear electrical conductivity were studied. The effect of anti-corona property of mixture of /spl beta/-SiC and /spl alpha/-SiC together with lacquer was discussed. Authors of this paper consider that the /spl beta/-SiC made from gangue could be used to replace /spl alpha/-SiC as anti-corona material.

articleTitle: Stress relieving with resistive materials based on silicon carbide (SiC)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: This article deals with stress relieving on components of high-voltage equipment with semi-conducting materials based on silicon carbide (SiC). By using SiC, non-linear resistance characteristics can be implemented. This is worthwhile where different operational states of a stress-relieving layer have to be implemented, e.g. in the case of housings for high-voltage fuses. Such housings may consist of a dielectric basic material with inner and outer conducting layers, where the outer layer is grounded and the inner layer is on high-voltage potential. The inner layer is of special interest, because it must comply with different tasks: When the fuse is in normal operation, the stress relieving must prevent partial discharge (PD) inside the fuse. If the fuse is open, the remaining current through the inner layer must be negligible. Two different types of conducting layers are discussed: one kind consists of a ceramic overglaze, the other is based on different organic mastics like silicon rubber, epoxy resin and silicon resin. SiC was used in different quantities, qualities and grain sizes, affecting the behavior of the conductive layer. The influences of these parameters are shown. The electrical behavior of both types of conductive layers, in dependence of various parameters like different voltage levels, temperature etc. will be presented. Finally the long-time behavior of these materials compared to materials already used in cables and cable accessories will be shown.

articleTitle: Structural changes in Ge-doped SiO/sub 2/ planar waveguides induced by ultraviolet photons
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: In this paper, we report the difference in absorption spectrum that has a close relation to photosensitivity and the improvement of the quality by thermal annealing between two Ge-doped SiO/sub 2/ planar waveguides synthesized by different methods.

articleTitle: Reduction of dielectric loss of sputtered tantalum oxide films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Dielectric properties (/spl epsiv/ and tan /spl delta/) of thin sputtered tantalum oxide films have been measured in the low frequency range. Anomalous large values of /spl epsiv/ and tan /spl delta/ have been observed at high temperatures above 100/spl deg/C. The heating of the substrate during the sputtering has a significant effect on the dielectric properties of the Ta oxide thin films. Samples prepared at substrate temperature above 200/spl deg/C show very low dielectric loss.

articleTitle: The total hydrocarbon ampere-volt method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: With overheating in the magnetic circuit, the total hydrocarbon content in a transformer is proportional to the square of the applied voltage while it is proportional to the square of the current when overheating occurs in the conductor circuit. In the paper, the total hydrocarbon ampere-volt method (THAVM) is introduced. The object of THAVM is to locate fault position by analyzing the relations between the total hydrocarbon content and the current or the applied voltage. It has proved this method is simple and economically feasible.

articleTitle: The study on on-line monitoring of fault discharge in large generators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: On-line monitoring of fault discharges is an important approach for indicating the condition of electrical insulation of large generators. In this paper, several key aspects of on-line monitoring systems are discussed, involving the characteristics of fault discharges in large generators, interference suppression, pattern recognition of fault discharges, and practical application of digital fault discharge on-line monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Influence of crystallinity on DC conduction in polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: Measurements of DC conduction current in high density polyethylene (HDPE) have been made. Based on the conduction mechanism of Richardson-Schottky field-aided electron injection, the conduction process of polyethylene with different crystallinity was mainly discussed.

articleTitle: Space charge behavior and electrical breakdown phenomena of acrylate-graft-polyethylenes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The space charge distribution and the impulse breakdown phenomena of acrylate-graft-polyethylenes, like acrylic acid and n-butylacrylate, were investigated. Heterocharges generated in low-density polyethylene were decreased with the introduction of acrylic acid and changed to homocharge formations with the increase of graft ratio. On the other hand, the space charge accumulation in n-butylacrylate grafted polyethylene remained unchanged for the whole range of the graft ratio. The impulse breakdown strength of the acrylate-graft-polyethylene was increased and changed according to the graft ratio.

articleTitle: Computation of horizontal three-phase line capacitances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 1998 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials. 1998 Asian International Conference on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. 30th Symposium on Electrical Insulating Ma
abstract: The author shows that it is possible to determine the horizontal three-phase line capacitance with the consideration of influences caused by the earth surface and ground wire. The computation results show that the increase in capacitance value caused by the ground wire is very small and can be neglected practically. For horizontal three-phase lines the capacitance of centre phase is much higher than the outer phases. This is very important and useful for the studies of corona, electric field, electrostatic imbalance of extra-high and ultra-high voltage transmission lines.
